title: Quandela and Hermes-Epitek Join Forces to Advance Photonic Quantum Technologies
html:
Insider Brief

  • Quandela and Hermes-Epitek have signed an MoU to explore the development and industrialisation of photonic quantum technologies through a proposed joint R&D programme.
  • The initial work will test an experimental platform in Taiwan combining Quandela’s single-photon sources and photonic integrated circuits with Hermes-Epitek’s superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors and cryogenic capabilities.
  • The companies may pursue a separate agreement to install a photonic quantum computer in Taiwan, with specifications, location, funding and timing still to be agreed.

PRESS RELEASE — Quandela and Hermes-Epitek Corporation (“Hermes-Epitek “) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at Hermes-Epitek’s premises in Hsinchu Science Park. The MoU outlines two companies’ intention to develop and industrialize photonic quantum technologies, beginning with a proposed joint R&D program. A subsequent phase would involve the installation of a quantum computer integrating technologies from both companies, subject to a separate agreement.

The joint program would combine Quandela’s semiconductor quantum-dot single-photon sources and photonic integrated circuits with Hermes-Epitek’s superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs), cryogenic capabilities, and photonic component manufacturing expertise. The two companies plan to begin by testing a joint experimental platform in Taiwan using fiber-coupled detectors, before exploring closer integration of detectors and photonic circuits.

Two companies also intend to negotiate a separate agreement for the installation and deployment of a photonic quantum computer in Taiwan incorporating technologies from both companies. The details of this future phase, including system specifications, the installation site, funding, and the timetable, remain subject to mutual agreement.

The collaboration aims to bring together Quandela’s quantum computing architecture and system integration expertise with Hermes-Epitek’s Taiwan-based capabilities in detector technology, semiconductor processing, and manufacturing. Subject to successful validation of the technologies, both companies will assess their suitability for future photonic quantum systems.

Mohib Ur Rehman

MENTIONED IN THE ARTICLE

Quandela is a French startup that specializes in photonic quantum computing by providing modular, scalable, and energy-efficient photonic quantum computers, accessible both on the cloud and on premise. They provide prototyping services with their Perceval simulator alongside their general purpose chips optimized chips, and development of algorithms and protocols which provide photonic solutions for applications ranging from pharmaceutical and material design, to quantum machine learning, networking and optimization.
